transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what really scared me enough to make an appointment is that I've started having these thoughts lately. I keep catching myself thinking that it would just be simpler if I didn't wake up tomorrow. I want to be clear that I don't have any actual plan to harm myself, but just having those thoughts at all was unsettling enough to make me realize I needed to talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been constant or come and go over time?

It’s been going on for about eight months now. It all started... well, it really began right around the time my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly. As for whether it comes and goes, it's been pretty much a constant feeling since then.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. I used to really enjoy painting, but lately... well, I still set out my watercolor things sometimes, hoping it will spark something. But I'll just sit there staring at the paper, and eventually I just put it all away. The pleasure I used to feel in the color and the light, it just doesn't seem to arrive anymore.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with racing thoughts or impulsive behavior?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never really had a time where I felt unusually energetic or... elated, I think you said. And I definitely haven't had days where I felt like I didn't need sleep, or where I was doing things impulsively. No, nothing like that at all.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up much earlier than you'd like?

Yes, my sleep has definitely changed. Getting to sleep is pretty uneven... sometimes I can, sometimes I can't. But the main issue is that I always seem to wake up around three or four in the morning. I just lie there thinking about all the things I need to do—phone calls I need to make, forms I have to fill out for my brother, worrying if I handled yesterday's issues correctly. Once my mind starts going like that, I can't get back to sleep. By the time morning actually rolls around, I feel like I've barely rested at all.
Have you ever had a similar period of low mood, loss of interest, or these kinds of symptoms at any other point earlier in your life, before the last eight months?

No, I haven't. This is the first time I've ever felt this way. I've had normal ups and downs, of course, but nothing that lasted this long or felt quite like this. Before these last eight months, I've always been pretty steady.
Over these past eight months, how has this been affecting your ability to keep up with daily responsibilities, like work, self-care, or managing things around the house?

Well, I'm still taking care of the essentials around the house. I get up, I eat, I manage the bills and look after my brother's things. But... I have pulled back from a lot of the extra things. I used to walk with a group, and I was doing some mentoring, but I've stopped. I just can't seem to follow through with it right now. When I'm around people, I just don't feel like I can be fully present the way I used to be. So I've just been keeping to myself more.
How often do these thoughts about not wanting to wake up occur, and how intense do they feel when they happen?

Well, they probably happen a few times a week now. Honestly, it's what scared me enough to finally come in and see someone. I've just started having these thoughts like... well, that it would be simpler if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. 

As for how intense they are, they don't feel overwhelming, and I want to be very clear that I don't have any sort of plan to actually harm myself. I wouldn't do that. It's just... having that thought at all was really unsettling for me, so I knew I needed to talk to a doctor.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions, even on simple everyday tasks, over these past eight months?

No, not really. I haven't had any trouble with my concentration. I mean, like I said, I still manage the bills and keep track of everything around the house just fine. Making decisions hasn't been an issue either. My mind still feels pretty clear, even if my mood is low, so... no, I haven't noticed any problems with that.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. My appetite has been about the same as usual, and my weight hasn't fluctuated or anything. I'm still eating my regular meals, so everything seems pretty normal in that regard.
Has your low mood affected your ability to work or fulfill your usual responsibilities to the point that you've had to cut back significantly or stop working altogether?

Well, I'm retired, so I don't have a job to go to, and like I mentioned, I still manage the bills and the house just fine. I take care of the essentials. But... I have pulled back from some of my other commitments. I used to be very involved with a walking group, and I did some mentoring, but I've stopped doing those things. I just can't seem to follow through on them anymore, or... or be fully present with people the way I used to be. So, the basic responsibilities are fine, but the extra things have definitely dropped off.
Over these past eight months, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven't been especially active?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have endless energy, but I wouldn't say I've been unusually tired or anything. I still have enough energy to get through the day and do what I need to do around the house. It's not a physical tiredness, it's more just... not wanting to do the extra things, like I said. But my actual energy levels seem pretty normal for me.
